Description: One row per economic category (127, plus Unknown), with its economic budget, PESA economic group and whether it runs as expenditure or income. The flow comes from the final digit of the code, with 12 authored exceptions (Flow Basis says which). Each category also carries the detail line of the income and expenditure statement it is added to (Statement Line Key, authored rules). Source view dw.v_model_account.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: the in-year outturn of each financial year against the restated annual (BUD) file, by vintage and level, with the gap, its share of the annual amount, the tolerance and the status. Only DEL at total level is graded; the other levels are recorded with their reason. Full-scope build only. Source view dw.v_model_annual_control (audit.bud_vs_inyear_del).
The control budget of a line: DEL, AME or Non-budget, with the five OSCAR detail codes under it (DEL PROG, DEL ADMIN, DEPT AME, NON-DEPT AME, NON-BUDGET). Source view dw.v_model_control_budget.

Office for National Statistics consumer price series, monthly: D7BT, the CPI index (2015 = 100), and D7G7, the annual rate (per cent). Read over the web from the two generator links pinned in the file manifest. The files are regenerated by the publisher each month, so the model can hold later months than the pinned copies. Not related to Fiscal Period: it reaches back to 1988, and a relationship would add a blank period. Real, published data; internet needed at refresh.

Rows of the two ONS CPI files that did not parse, with the file and the reason. Empty when every row parses (tested by tests/dax/705). Annual and quarterly rows are not loaded and are not failures; a row of any other shape after the data starts, a value that is not a number or a month out of order lands here.

The data-quality findings the build records: a unit error in the NHS Pension Scheme lines, a wrong quarter label, the June 2019 period 0 rows and a coding error. Fact Outturn points at a finding where it flags rows; every other row points at the member No issue flagged, which is a label and holds no amount. Source view dw.v_model_data_quality.

HM Treasury GDP deflators at market prices (2025-26 = 100), one row per financial year and vintage, read over the web from the three workbooks pinned in the file manifest and parsed by header text in Power Query. Forecast years have no published index: Chained Index carries the published level for outturn years and, for forecast years, the level chained from the year before with its published per cent change (four decimals at each step), so real terms use one vintage throughout. Default vintage: October 2026 Budget. Rows that fail to parse are in Deflator Quarantine. Real, published data; internet needed at refresh.

Rows of the three GDP deflator workbooks that did not parse, with the file and the reason. Empty when every row parses (tested by tests/dax/705). Nothing is dropped silently: a row that is neither a financial-year row nor a blank or note line lands here.

The departments of today's structure (63 members: 59 departments and 4 Unallocated members for lines of closed or split departments that no current department took over). Fact Outturn joins on the current-department key written in the warehouse, so every line sits in exactly one department, restated onto the current structure with no weights. Source view dw.v_model_department.

Calculation group that shows an amount in GBP thousands, millions or billions. It divides the value (the data is in GBP thousands) and sets a dynamic format string with the unit suffix; no number format scales with commas. It acts on the amount measures only (the base, plan, comparison and statement amounts), leaves percentages and indicators unscaled, and gives Variance %, YoY % and Favourable/Adverse their own formats. Precedence 30: the outermost, so its format string is the one that applies when a unit is selected.

DERIVED from real data, in GBP thousands (not pounds): how well each forecast of the monthly returns scored against the final outturn (R13). One row per forecast line, department group, budget measure, financial year, return and method. The department's own forecasts are the real returns; the run rate, seasonal and FTE x cost methods are my own forecasts, made from only what was known at the return, and every score is computed from them in SQL. The forecast line is a budget measure total (RDEL, CDEL or AME, three methods) or the pay line (A101 of RDEL, four methods: FTE x cost exists only here and only where the department's workforce is published for the month). Known Bad Return marks a department group's whole return that is flagged (a units error, a scale outlier, a body or department missing); every measure has a version without those returns. Scored By Every Method marks the cells that every method of the line scored, the cells on which the methods compare like for like. Nothing synthetic or authored is in it. Ratios are ratios of sums, never averages of percentages. The department is the department of the current structure that the group's department number maps to, so the security roles filter it through Department (current structure). Source view dw.v_model_forecast_accuracy.

Real outturn from the 31 OSCAR in-year releases as revision deltas: one row for each change a release makes to a line (organisation version, sub-segment, economic category, control budget detail, period), only non-zero deltas. The sum of the deltas up to a release equals what that release reports. GBP thousands, spending positive, income negative. Source view dw.v_model_fact_outturn.

DERIVED from real data, in pounds (not GBP thousands): the paybill and full-time equivalent of the payroll published in the departments' monthly workforce files, compared month against the same month a year earlier. One row per department of the current structure, organisation and month (the later month of the two). A row is continuing (valid in both months in the same department), entry, exit, or not_bridged (left out, with a reason); only the first three enter the bridge. Valid means the cell has a full-time equivalent above zero and a paybill above zero, and no published row behind it is listed in audit.workforce_row_arithmetic. Nothing synthetic or authored is in it; the only authored input is the map from a published name to an organisation. The department is the department of the current structure the body sat in that month, so the security roles filter it through Department (current structure). Source view dw.v_model_pay_bridge.

Real plans as published, at the grain of their source (see Plan Grain): OSCAR Plans by organisation to 2021-22, Estimates by Spending Review group from 2022-23, PESA departmental AME and administration budgets by group to 2028-29. Held for the year, not by month; compare with outturn only at the plan's grain or coarser. GBP thousands. Source view dw.v_model_fact_plan.

DERIVED, not published: each plan row spread over periods 1 to 12 by a share taken from the prior year's outturn (or twelve flat twelfths where there is none). The monthly plan is my allocation of a published annual figure; the twelve rows of a plan row add up to it exactly. Scenario is Plan (phased), which is flagged derived. It never enters a real total and must never be shown as a published monthly budget. Source view dw.v_model_fact_plan_phased.

Real data, as published: the statutory income statement, balance sheet and cash flow of every NHS trust and foundation trust, FY2019-20 to FY2024-25, one row per provider, file year, statement line and column (current or prior year), 344,812 rows, in GBP thousands on the TAC sign (income, assets and inflows positive; expenses, liabilities and outflows negative), which is not the OSCAR sign. A subtotal or total is in the data as a value: the measures add only lines of kind line, and show a subtotal only on its own row. Related to the provider, which carries the department of the current structure, so the security roles filter it. Source view dw.v_model_tac_fact.

DERIVED, not published: the indirect cash flow of every NHS provider and year, built from the income statement and the balance sheet (the movement of each balance-sheet line, current year less prior year of the same file, and the flows of the income statement) through the authored map authored/tac_cash_flow_map.csv. GBP thousands, TAC sign, one row per provider, year and derived line. The inputs are real; the result is my calculation, it is compared with the published cash flow and never forced to equal it, and it never enters a real total. Source view dw.v_model_tac_cash_flow_derived.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: one row per OSCAR in-year release file with the rows the load read, loaded and quarantined, the file's own total as the text the control produced and as four decimals, and a measure that sets the model's as-at outturn of the release's own year beside the file total. Source view dw.v_model_file_control (audit.file_control).

One row per financial year and period: period 1 is April, period 12 is March. Period 0 holds amounts the source does not allocate to a month (71 rows of the June 2019 release) and counts in year totals. There is no calendar date table and no auto date/time. Source view dw.v_model_fiscal_period.

One row per UK financial year (April to March), 2017-18 to 2028-29. 2017-18 has plans (OSCAR Plans) and no outturn, because the in-year releases start at 2018-19. The plan is published by year, so Fact Plan relates here; Fiscal Period relates here too, which gives outturn and plan one year slicer. Source view dw.v_model_fiscal_year.

Labels only, no number: the four forecast methods and what each one is. The department's own forecast is the real return; run rate, seasonal and FTE x cost are my own methods (FTE x cost is for the pay line only). Source view dw.v_model_forecast_method.

Labels only, no number: the returns that are scored, R0 (before the year, nothing actual) to R12 (twelve months actual). R13 is the final outturn they are scored against and is not a row here. Source view dw.v_model_forecast_return.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: the rows read, loaded and quarantined of every in-year release file and every annual restated file, and two counts of the rows that the web-read deflator and CPI loads rejected. Nothing is dropped silently: a rejected row is counted here and kept in a quarantine table. Full-scope build only. Source view dw.v_model_load_control (audit.file_control and audit.bud_file_control).

One row per version of an organisation (Type 2, 408 versions plus Unknown): a new version starts when the code, the department or the name really changes. Fact Outturn joins here on the version the release used, so this is the structure as each release reported it. The department columns say which department that version sat under. Source view dw.v_model_organisation.

Labels only, no number: the five steps of the pay bridge waterfall (prior paybill, volume, rate, mix, entry and exit), so that one measure (Pay Bridge Step Amount) can give each step its value. Source view dw.v_model_pay_bridge_step.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: for each department series and month of the workforce files, how many published rows the organisation map placed on an organisation, and the full-time equivalent and paybill (pounds) published and placed. The mapped share is the coverage the pay bridge rests on: 93.8 per cent of published payroll full-time equivalent and 76.8 per cent of paybill overall. The Ministry of Defence's paybill is 45.5 per cent covered (rows labelled another month are quarantined) and the core of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government is not mapped. Related to the fiscal period only; not filtered by the department roles and hidden from the Restricted Viewer. Source view dw.v_model_pay_coverage (audit.workforce_mapping_coverage).

One row per organisation that appears in the monthly workforce files (89 of them), with the code and the name of its latest version. A body that moved department over the period is one row here; the fact carries the department it sat in each month. Hidden from the Restricted Viewer: it is the organisation-level identity of paybill. Source view dw.v_model_pay_organisation.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: what the plan fact holds for each plan source, financial year, plan measure and grain, with the number of fact rows, the number of lines in the source sheet and the total. It is how a reader sees which year is published at which grain. Source view dw.v_model_plan_coverage (dw.plan_coverage).

AUTHORED list, no amount: the four grains a plan is published at (A OSCAR organisation, B Estimates group, C Estimates 2022-23, D PESA group). A plan can be compared with outturn only at its own grain or coarser. Source view dw.v_model_plan_grain.

AUTHORED descriptions of published files, no amount: each source and edition a plan comes from: OSCAR Plans, the Estimates workbooks, PESA editions and Spending Review 2025. Carries the basis, whether Scotland is before or after the block grant adjustment and whether the edition is the final plan of its year. Authored descriptions of published files. Source view dw.v_model_plan_source.

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: every plan variance from FY2022-23, one row for each financial year, Spending Review group and plan measure (resource DEL excluding depreciation, capital DEL, departmental resource AME and capital AME), with the independent outturn, the part of the variance each named cause accounts for, the residual and a verdict (ok, fixed, explained with its reason, or unexplained). Amounts in GBP thousands, spending positive; variance is outturn on the plan's basis less plan. Not related to any other table, so no selection reaches it. Full-scope build only. Source view dw.v_model_plan_variance (audit.plan_variance_reconciliation).

AUDIT and CONTROL, no new number: the Public Spending Statistics database against OSCAR outturn by financial year, Spending Review group and measure (resource DEL excluding depreciation, capital DEL), with the gap and the graded total rows. The known capital DEL gaps of 2023-24 and 2024-25 are in it, not hidden. Full-scope build only. Source view dw.v_model_pss_control (audit.pss_vs_outturn).

One row per OSCAR in-year release (March 2019 to September 2026, 31 in all). Each release restates the year to date, and Fact Outturn stores the change since the previous release of the same year, so the release is how a view as at a point in time is built. Source view dw.v_model_release.

AUTHORED list, no amount: the five scenarios the model compares: Outturn and Plan (published), Plan (phased) and Own forecast (derived), and Departments' forecast (published). Only Outturn, Plan and Plan (phased) carry rows today. Source view dw.v_model_scenario.

Calculation group for comparing outturn with plan: Actual, Plan, Variance, Variance % and Favourable/Adverse. It acts on the measures Comparison Amount and Statement Amount only (any other measure passes through), so it can be dropped on a visual of any other measure without changing it. Sign convention: spending positive, income negative, so Actual less Plan below zero is favourable for both. Precedence 10: the innermost of the three calculation groups, so Time Intelligence and Display Unit wrap it.

AUTHORED names and mapping, no amount: the 23 Spending Review groups of the latest annual release plus the members that plans and outturn need: the Single Intelligence Account (plan only), the combined pre-2023 group of BEIS, DCMS and DIT, six non-department members and one outturn-only member for former department lines. Plans are published by group, and outturn reaches the group through the bridge built from the current-structure department. Authored names and types, no amount. Source view dw.v_model_sr_group.

AUTHORED layout of the group income and expenditure statement: one row per line (detail, subtotal, total or spacer), in the order it prints, with the sign it is presented in, its indent, the lines it adds up and the plan scope it is compared with. I wrote the layout (authored/statement_line.csv); no row holds an amount. Account is related to it, so a detail line filters the accounts it adds up. Source view dw.v_model_statement_line.

AUTHORED field parameter, no amount: field parameter for the statement: Outturn, Plan, Variance and Variance % of the statement amount, so that one visual can switch between them. Each row points at a measure (Statement Amount, Statement Plan, Statement Variance, Statement Variance %). I defined it in the model; putting it on a visual needs one step in Desktop that pbir cannot do (remove the field, drag the parameter back in), and the report uses the Scenario Comparison items instead where it can. Calculated table, no source data.
One row per OSCAR sub-segment code (3,765, plus Unknown): the finest spending line the source reports. Source view dw.v_model_segment.

AUTHORED labels, no amount: the lines of the derived indirect cash flow, in three published sections (operating, investing, financing) and one of reserve movements that have no cash counterpart, each with whether it is compared with published lines, exists only on the derived side or only on the published side. A published cash-flow line points at the derived line it is compared with, so one line here filters both the derived amount and the published lines it is set against. The member Not compared is every other statement line. Source view dw.v_model_tac_cash_flow_line, from authored/tac_cash_flow_line.csv.

AUTHORED, hand-keyed: the values printed in the consolidated NHS provider accounts (the statements in which intra-NHS balances are eliminated), eight printed lines for each of the six years, in GBP million as printed, with the printed and PDF page of each and the figure the next year's report gives for the same year. The only authored amounts of the TAC objects; the elimination gap compares them with the provider sum and no total adds them to a provider amount. Source view dw.v_model_tac_consolidated, from authored/tac_consolidated_control.csv.

AUTHORED labels, no amount: the six headline lines of the elimination-gap control (total operating income, operating expenses, total assets, total liabilities, cash and total assets employed), whether each is a flow of the year or a balance at its end. Source view dw.v_model_tac_control_line, from authored/tac_control_line.csv.
AUTHORED, hidden, no amount: which statement lines (never a subtotal or a total) make up each control line. Read by the measure TAC Provider Sum (control). Source view dw.v_model_tac_control_member.

The NHS trusts and foundation trusts in the TAC files, one row per NHS (ODS) code, 228 in all, with the provider's latest name, type, region and sector (real, from the published lists of providers), the years it has statements, and where it went when it was acquired, merged or dissolved (authored: hand-written from the source's own comments, each with a quotation the build checks). Every provider is linked to the Department of Health and Social Care, which is how the security roles reach the TAC facts. Source view dw.v_model_tac_provider.

The 137 lines of the three statutory statements the NHS providers file: income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, with the text and sign of the form (real, from the illustrative forms), and for each line its section and whether it is a line, a subtotal or a total (authored: the form computes a subtotal from other lines, so adding it to its components counts it twice). Holds no amount. Source view dw.v_model_tac_line.

Calculation group for fiscal-period time intelligence on Fiscal Period and Fiscal Year: Current, MTD, QTD, YTD, PY, YoY, YoY % and Rolling 12 months. No calendar date table and no calendar time-intelligence functions: a window is a set of Fiscal Period rows. Period 0 (not allocated to a month) is in year totals and the year to date and never in a single month. Precedence 20: outside Scenario Comparison (so Variance % of YTD is the variance of the year-to-date amounts, not a year-to-date of the percentages) and inside Display Unit.

SYNTHETIC, hidden, no amount: invented users (example.org addresses) and the departments of the current structure each may see. Read only by the row-level security roles, which filter the department dimension to the rows of USERPRINCIPALNAME(). It filters data and holds none, so no real total reads it. Source view dw.v_model_user_department, from synthetic/user_department.csv.

SYNTHETIC, hidden, no amount: the Spending Review groups whose plan an invented user may see, which are the groups all of whose departments are among the user's departments. Read only by the row-level security roles, which filter the plan facts to these groups. It filters data and holds none, so no real total reads it. Source view dw.v_model_user_plan_group, from synthetic/user_department.csv.
